themes_detail.label: Street Condition Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints spiked to 62 THIS WEEK, a 282% jump from the 16.2-week average, suggesting acute pavement, pothole, or surface deterioration across Midwood/Ocean Parkway warranting urgent investigation into whether weather, construction, or deferred maintenance is responsible.
evidence: 62 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs 16.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.06)
282% spike represents the most acute street infrastructure crisis in recent baseline data
Temporally aligned with street sign damage spike (5 complaints 2 weeks ago vs 0.5 avg), suggesting broader street infrastructure failure
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: photodocument the worst streets in Midwood and Ocean Parkway; interview residents about impact on safety, vehicles, accessibility
DOT accountability: request street inspection records, repair timelines, and budget allocation for CD314 vs other districts

themes_detail.label: Encampment Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 967% spike from the 0.4-week baseline, indicating either new or rapidly visible homelessness/informal settlements in Midwood that may signal either a crisis response or coordinated relocation from elsewhere in the city.
evidence: 4 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.21, 967% spike)
First major encampment signal in recent baseline data; represents emergence or visibility change
Aligns temporally with residential disposal spike (28 complaints last week), potentially indicating overflow sanitation issues from encampments
reporting_angles: On-ground reporting: locate and assess encampments in Midwood; interview residents and unhoused individuals about services, barriers, relocation history
City response: request DSS/DSNY protocols for CD314; investigate whether this is organic growth or result of sweeps/relocations elsewhere

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks Spike
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints peaked at 6 THREE WEEKS AGO (1500% above 0.4-week baseline, z-score 11.62), marking the highest statistical anomaly in the dataset, though timing suggests this may be holiday-related; requires verification of whether this spike persisted or resolved.
evidence: 6 illegal fireworks complaints 3 weeks ago vs 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 11.62, 1500% spike — highest anomaly in dataset)
Likely holiday-correlated but requires current-week data to confirm resolution
No follow-up data available to determine if spike was temporary or indicative of ongoing problem
reporting_angles: Quick turnaround: check with NYPD 70th Precinct on illegal fireworks enforcement and whether complaints have returned to baseline
Context: if sustained, investigate whether fireworks are tied to organized activity or neighborhood culture; interview affected residents about noise/safety impact

themes_detail.label: Residential Waste Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints spiked to 28 LAST WEEK, a 446% jump from the 5.1-week baseline, suggesting acute trash/waste overflow or sanitation system failure; likely interconnected with encampment spike and unsanitary condition complaints (953 total over 90 days).
evidence: 28 residential disposal complaints LAST WEEK vs 5.1 weekly average (z-score: 7.19, 446% spike)
Converges with encampment spike (4 complaints THIS WEEK) and unsanitary condition complaints (953 over 90 days), suggesting systemic sanitation breakdown
Root/sewer/sidewalk condition also spiked (5 complaints last week vs 1.2 avg), indicating infrastructure-level waste handling issues
reporting_angles: DSNY accountability: request collection schedules, missed pickups, and service disruptions in CD314; investigate whether staffing shortages or route changes caused spike
Resident impact: document overflowing bins, street-level trash, and health/pest concerns; interview block associations

themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 57 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 356% spike from 12.5-week baseline, indicating acute construction, commercial activity, or traffic disruption; requires verification of whether this has persisted into this week.
evidence: 57 street/sidewalk noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs 12.5 weekly average (z-score: 8.41, 356% spike)
Distinct from residential noise (1825 complaints over 90 days), indicating external/commercial source
Temporally aligned with street sign damage spike (5 complaints 2 weeks ago), suggesting active street-level disruption (construction, activity, infrastructure work)
reporting_angles: DOB/construction audit: cross-reference 293 recent building permits (221 alterations) with noise complaint hotspots; identify active construction sites and verify noise compliance
Resident impact: interview affected blocks on Ocean Parkway and key corridors about noise source, duration, and impact on sleep/commerce
